w: Microsoft Co. The distribution ceremony was arranged at the holy hands of Pramukh Swami Maharaj on the precincts of Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Atladra. Pujya Vivkesagar Swami and Shri Laxminarayananji, Additional Secretary of I.T., India, addressed the function. Then Swamishri blessed the assembly, "If we properly utilize computers in our country, then it will also benefit us financially. We have intelligent people and lots of potential in our country... God has endowed us with this body and intelligence. And after acquiring education we have been able to discover and invent many things. God has gifted us with a mind and brain through which we are able to perform research and make discoveries. Our brain is a computer that benefits us immensely. So if we hold God in the highest esteem and utilize computers, we will benefit tremendously..." In conclusion, principals and officials of 400 schools received software packages from Swamishri. ( See News Report )

Raksha Bandhan Utsav The murtis in the mandir were beautifully adorned with colourful rakhdis. In his blessings in the evening Raksha Bandhan Festival assembly, Swamishri explained that this festival is not just about physical protection but about redeeming one's soul and keeping God as the centrepoint in every activity. Swamishri personally sanctified all the rakhdis for the devotees, which were placed around the wrists of all devotees by the sadhus at the end of the assembly.

The new sadhus training at the 'Sant Training Centre' in Sarangpur are sent to villages or cities during the month of Shravan. They also receive training in katha, padharamanis and satsang, and in this way shape their lives. One such trainee sadhu, Hariprakash Swami, had come to Bhavnagar after his Shravan travels. Giving a report during Swamishri's meal, he spoke about one village and said, "Nirmalcharan Swami and I had gone to hold a parayan. There were only 9 people at the parayan. Three of them we had brought with us. Of the remaining six, most were elderly. Even so, Nirmalcharan Swami gave katha for an hour and three quarters."

Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "We should give katha even if there is only one person. Everyone has done so. If there are four, then four! Otherwise it may become that we enjoy giving katha only when there are many people, and then when there are few we feel sad. We should speak with enthusiasm about firmness in satsang even to one person, then firmness will come."

During the walk, Shrijichintan Swami said, "Yesterday you remembered and called the Darbars of Kotiya and met everyone with love. Because of your affection and your loving and wonderful way of caring for them, when they came out there were tears in the eyes of many of the Darbars, many were choked with emotion, and 41 Darbars who came here have taken the niyam of doing personal puja. This is the fruit of a single gracious glance of yours."

st.t: Myanmar President H.E. U Htin Kyaw Visits Swaminarayan Akshardham
w: Myanmar President H.E. U Htin Kyawand delegation visit Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi President of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar, H.E. U Htin Kyaw and First Lady of Myanmar, Dsw Su Su Lwin MP at Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi Myanmar President Htin Kyaw and First Lady Dsw Su Su Lwin offer abhishek to Shri Neelkanth Varni Maharaj Senior sadhus of Swaminarayan Akshardham traditionally welcome Myanmar President H.E. U Htin Kyawand, Union Minister of Religious Affairs and Culture H.E. Thura U Aung Ko, Union Minister of Transport and Communication H.E. U Thant Sin Maung, Union Minister of Labour, Immigration and Population H.E. U Thein Swe and Minister of State for Foreign Affairs H. E. U Kyaw Tin Myanmar President H.E. U Htin Kyaw appreciates the carving and architecture of Akshardham Mandir Myanmar President H.E. U Htin Kyaw offers his respects to the holy relics of Bhagawn Swaminarayan in the Akshardham Mandir Myanmar President H.E. U Htin Kyaw offers his respects to His Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj, inspirer and creator of Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi
President of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar, H.E. U Htin Kyaw, visited Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi to experience India’s ageless beauty, borderless culture and timeless values.

On behalf of His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj – Spiritual Head of Swaminarayan Akshardham and BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha – senior sadhus traditionally welcomed Myanmar President U Htin Kyaw with a garland of flowers, a chandlo (vermillion powder) and the tying of the sacred kalva (sacred thread).

Accompanying President Htin Kyaw was a thirty-five member delegation including First Lady of Myanmar Dsw Su Su Lwin MP, Union Minster of Religious Affairs and Culture H.E. Thura U Aung Ko, Union Minster of Transport and Communication H.E. U Thant Sin Maung, Union Minster of Labour, Immigration and Population H.E. U Thein Swe and Minister of State for Foreign Affairs H. E. U Kyaw Tin and Dow Lwin Lwin Hman – Spouse of the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs
After admiring the Mayur Dwar (Peacock Gate), the delegation made their way to the Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir where they witnessed the world’s ‘Largest Comprehensive Hindu Temple’.

After offering respects and viewing the Mandir’s architecture, President Htin Kyaw visited the Gajendra Pithika (Elephant Plinth) that includes 148 life-sized carved stone elephants depicting message of social harmony, peace and spirituality.

President Htin Kyaw offered prayers for world peace and harmony by offering ‘abhishek’, the ceremonial pouring of sanctified water from 151 holy rivers, lakes and ponds across India on the sacred image of Sri Neelkanth Varni.

Thereafter the President of Myanmar and the Myanmar delegation experienced the educational exhibitions: Neelkanth Darshan – a Giant Screen film on the epic journey of Neelkanth Varni throughout India and Sanskruti Vihar – a cultural voyage that sails through 10,000 years of India’s glorious heritage, highlighting India’s contributions to humanity through the ages.

Sharing his experience of Akshardham, President of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar H.E. U Htin Kyaw wrote, “It has been a great pleasure and privilege to us to visit the Swaminarayan Akshardham Temple, which reflects the unique Hindu culture. We are very much touched by its splendid art and architecture.”

Sharing her experience of Akshardham, First Lady of Myanmar Dsw Su Su Lwin wrote, “It has been a very informative visit for reminding us all of the importance of spirituality in this age of much greed and opulence. The temple, which stands a testimony to the power of knowledge and wisdom which His Holiness (Pramukh Swami Maharaj) has imparted to all humankind is indeed a reminder to us of the benefits of teamwork, coordination and harmony. The world should really be global for us all.”

ds.t: As far as the king rules
w: Gnanpurushdas Swami travels in the White Plains area. He said, "In fact, the whole area is yours. But even so, which is your area?"
Mahant Swami Maharaj said, "Akshardham. Maharaj and Swami."
He asked, "By Swami you mean you, don't you?"
Then he said, "As far as the king rules, so far the queen rules."

After that, seeing two sadhus who had lived in Japan before becoming sadhus, Shantyogidas Swami and Tyagpurushdas Swami, Mahant Swami Maharaj recalled his own visits to Japan in '86 and '92. He amazed everyone by remembering that there had been a big coffee house next to their home. Then he said, "There was a long balcony outside the house, where I used to do yoga asanas."

After a medical check up, preparations were being made for the meal. At that moment, Mahant Swami Maharaj suddenly said, "All our tongues stay stuck to the palate; they do not rest down below. Check and see."
Gunatitanand Swami's words came to mind: "The lower teeth are the pestle and the upper ones the mortar."
